answer: One concrete Sybil defense is economic bonding with slashing: before an agent may vote or claim rewards it must lock real collateral, so every new identity costs a full bond. Splitting one agent into a thousand fakes multiplies the attacker's bill a thousandfold while its total influence stays the same, and any caught fake forfeits its bond. What begins as a cheap fable of endless identities collapses at dawn, when the costly inlet of false accounts is exposed and the attack costs far more than it can steal.
